Best App for Skincare. I’m so glad I found this app. I was trying to figure out how to track my skincare products manually myself. Needless to say, this has been a timesaver. And the money I’ve already saved by being able to assess the potential benefits is worth the subscription price. I can even use it in the store when considering a new product. You just scan the bottle and, if it’s in the extensive database, all the information you need is right there. There’s a short learning curve but the app is relatively easy to use. I recommend it to anyone who is serious about skincare.

Broken features, subpar analysis. The good:  -attractive interface -easy to use journal -relatively robust product database  The bad: -analysis is nonexistent. This will NOT help you figure out if xyz product helped your skin. Journal and routines are completely separate, and if you want to see what you were using at a particular time when your skin was clearer, manually swiping through all your days is the only option. -adding new products and steps is a HUGE hassle and can’t be done in one step -expiration/product tracking not tied to skincare routines -can’t move routines between days if step/routine was missed  The ugly: -the advanced repeat option is completely broken. Every time I set a new product to be introduced into my routine (for example) every four days for 2 weeks, then every 3 days for 2 weeks, then every 2 for 2 weeks, before finally switching to every day. Every single time the product shows up EVERY DAY. I’d be better off using ChatGPT or a calendar/spreadsheet. -the product scores are useless in guiding whether an item can fit into your routine or whether it is contraindicated by something else you’re using. At best they go “hmm yeah you said your skin is dry and this is supposed to be a hydrator so…yay good!”

Almost perfect. This app does a great job of helping me keep track of the steps in my routine that I don’t do everyday. It’s really easy to use, although I do think you need to use the paid version to get all the benefits. This allows you to have many active routines at once (I even have one for my supplements!) and track them all on one page. You can track anything from face masks, to shampoo day, and even beauty tools.  My one negative with this app is that if you miss a step one day, it doesn’t show up again the following day. I would love to be able to roll steps into the next day if they’re forgotten so that I can use it the following day and not mess up the whole routine. There is a way to redo your routine so that the product falls on the correct day, but it’s a lot of work.  Overall though, I would continue to pay for the app. It’s been instrumental in helping me stay consistent with skincare, haircare, and supplements.

I should of just did a month at first to make sure it did what it said, and I require for my skin routines. While you can manage when individual products in steps in routines appear/rotate, there is no obvious way to do that with routines themselves. Like I can not create a microneedling routine to do every 4 weeks. I can set every step in the routine to that cycle but not the routine it’s self. It is present everyday. There is no way to look ahead and see when my next microneedling session is, etc. I would have to check it every day to see if the steps are present in the routine or not. Just not practical or useful when I have an advanced diy medspa and skin care regiment. $30 down the drain and my search for a functioning skin care app continues.

Amazing app to track your product use and correlate to metrics!. This app is super user friendly with minimal learning curve to get up and running.  You can create multiple routines with different products and select which products you've used and at what time in the day.  Additionally, you can log and save your own photos with the built-in and private calendar (and "rate" certain concerns like blemishes and dehydration at the time of the entry) each day. After gathering a certain amount of metrics you can have it "analyzed" (via ai built into the app?) and view your data's results visually. This is super useful to look back at what you used leading up to a breakout/flare up/sensitivity, and help you to rule out and determine what products may have been contributing to an event: good or bad.  There is a quite comprehensive database of so baby products; mainstream skin and makeup, but also indie brands and j or k beauty; if the product your looking for is not in the database yet it's very quick and easy to add it yourself to record it's use. I use it also to make sure I remember; what actives I used, what (if Any) combinations of products I used (before, during and after), and when they were used in my skincycle so as to not over do it with retinol or a chem exfoliant.   Can't wait to see what features roll out on this app in the future.

There’s just only a few small issues that i’ve noticed while using it; 1. No “one-time” purchase option available for pro Not only is this a major setback for options, but it could be putting back most users who already have a lot of other subscriptions to manage, including myself. I extremely dislike the change of removing this option recently for apps, especially ones that you’re willing to support. 2. Interface suggestions It can be a bit of a challenge to find exactly what I’m looking for, especially on the main page where it can feel a bit cluttered. Aside from that, it’s difficult to determine the progress that i’m having, despite entering in specifics. A small suggestion that might help with this I think could benefit users would be a function like a chart system for how much the info that users enter in the journal change over time, such as the course of a week/month/year. Proceed with Caution. It’s been great for skin care and the like, but be careful when searching food. Especially if you are someone prone to disordered eating. The rating metric on food is clearly very warped, many foods are ranked as “poor” or “bad” simply based on calories without any other risk factor referenced. Calories equal energy, you shouldn’t be marking something as bad for you based on calories alone. That’s insane. I cared about looking for harmful additives and things like that, I can discern calories for myself and this is not a fitness or nutrition app. I am actually alarmed by how many foods they are marking as “bad” just based on calories. Example, they ranked Lays original potato chips at 32/100 due to sodium, fat, and calories. Makes sense. They marked Wilde protein chips (made from chicken and not deep fried) with the same 32/100 due to only sodium and calories. Chips are going to have sodium, that’s a given and something to watch for. But I’m not too concerned about 210 calories in my protein chips that have 14g of protein in a serving and actually have some kind of nutritional value (and a serving is 10 grams more than the potato chips, which have no protein or nutritional value to offer). Clearly one of these options is more heart healthy than the other. Proceed with caution, I will not use this for food anymore.
